question: A 2019 review warned insects could nearly vanish within a century. Why did other ecologists distrust its method?
options: It searched only for studies of decline
It relied on data from before 1950
answer: It searched only for studies of decline. Sánchez-Bayo and Wyckhuys found their papers by searching a database with the word decline, so studies showing stable or rising numbers were mostly left out. Komonen and colleagues called it alarmist by design. Real declines exist, but a net cast for losses catches losses.
move: Ask how the evidence was gathered before asking what it says.
ask: When I look things up, do I search for the answer I already expect?
trap: A review of many studies seems balanced simply because it is big.
reference: Komonen, Halme & Kotiaho, Alarmist by bad design: strongly popularized unsubstantiated claims undermine credibility of conservation science, Rethinking Ecology, 2019; Sánchez-Bayo & Wyckhuys, Worldwide decline of the entomofauna: a review of its drivers, Biological Conservation, 2019
